    <title>On $κ$-existentially closed groups with few automorphisms</title>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39690v1</id>
    <title>Large Ree groups acting point and line-primitively on finite generalised quadrangles</title>
    <updated>2026-10-29T09:30:59Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39690v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39690v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Suppose we have a finite thick generalised quadrangle whose automorphism group $G$ acts primitively on both the set of points and the set of lines. Then $G$ must be almost simple. Furthermore, $\textrm{soc}(G)$ cannot be isomorphic to ${}^2 B_2(2^{2m+1})$ or ${}^2 G_2(3^{2m+1})$, where $m$ is a positive integer. In this paper, we show that $\textrm{soc}(G)$ cannot be isomorphic to ${}^2 F_4(2^{2m+1})$.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-29T09:30:59Z</published>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39673v1</id>
    <title>Random semigroups á la Gromov</title>
    <updated>2026-10-29T09:22:27Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39673v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39673v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We introduce a model of random semigroups analogous to Gromov's density model for random groups. For a fixed number $n\ge 2$ of generators and a density parameter $δ\in (0,1)$, we impose a uniformly chosen set of $\lfloor n^{2δl}\rfloor$ relations of the form $u=v$, where $u,v$ are distinct words of length at most $l$, and study the resulting semigroup as $l\to\infty$. We prove that, with overwhelming probability, above density $1/2$ the semigroup is trivial, while below density $1/2$ it contains a free subsemigroup of rank two, has a Golod-Shafarevich semigroup algebra over every field, and has a homomorphic image which generates a non-elementary hyperbolic group. We also show that the small cancellation condition $C(m)$ holds with overwhelming probability whenever $δ<1/2m$. Finally, for $n\ge 3$, at critical density $1/2$ we obtain a subsequential limiting distribution on finite semigroups, with positive mass at the trivial semigroup and unbounded support in size. This contrasts with random groups, which have order at most two with overwhelming probability at critical density.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.PR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39487v1</id>
    <title>Epimorphism testing with dihedral targets</title>
    <updated>2026-10-29T06:51:02Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39487v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39487v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We consider the problem of deciding whether or not there is an epimorphism from the class of finitely presented groups to a fixed finite group. We show this problem is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete when the target is a non-nilpotent dihedral group. This complements work of Kuperberg and Samperton (2018, Geom. Topol.) who showed the same result when the target is a fixed finite non-abelian simple group. We also include a survey of complexity and reduction results when the source and target are classes of finitely presented groups.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39463v1</id>
    <title>Subindices of two-element subsets of finite groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-29T06:34:50Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39463v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39463v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let $A$ be a nonempty subset of a group $G$. A right subfactor relative to $A$ is a subset $B$ maximal under inclusion among those for which every element of $AB$ has a unique representation as $ab$, with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$. Left subfactors are defined analogously using $BA$. The infima and suprema of the cardinalities of right and left subfactors define four \emph{subindices}. A subset is called \emph{index-stable} if its four subindices coincide.
  For any infinite group $G$, every nonempty finite subset of $G$ is index-stable.
  For finite groups, the situation is more complicated. We prove that for a two-element subset of a finite group, the left and right subindices coincide pairwise. Let $A=\{x,y\}$ with $x\ne y$, and let $X$ be the cyclic subgroup generated by $x^{-1}y$. Then the lower subindex of $A$ is $|G:X|\cdot\lceil |X|/3\rceil$, and the upper subindex is $|G:X|\cdot\lfloor |X|/2\rfloor$. These formulas imply that $A$ is index-stable if and only if $|X|$ is one of $2,3,4,5,7$.
  For any two-element subset of a finite group $G$, the lower subindex is at least $\lceil |G|/3\rceil$, and the upper subindex is at most $\lfloor |G|/2\rfloor$. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in each of these bounds.
  All two-element subsets of a finite group are index-stable if and only if every element of the group has order $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$, $5$, or $7$. We give a complete structural classification of such groups.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-29T06:34:50Z</published>

    </author>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39407v1</id>
    <title>Complete regular dessins and non-metacyclic bicyclic 2-groups with cyclic commutator subgroup</title>
    <updated>2026-10-29T05:44:15Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39407v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39407v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We study complete regular dessins with underlying graph ${\mathcal K}_{2^e,2^f}$, where $e\geq f\geq 2$, whose automorphism groups are non-metacyclic. Together with the cases of coprime orders and odd-prime-power orders, this is one of the basic classes needed for Jones's open classification problem for regular dessins of complete bipartite graphs. Within the 2-power case, the present paper treats the subcase in which the commutator subgroup is cyclic; it is the first of three papers devoted to the non-metacyclic case.
  Our approach is group-theoretic. The automorphism group $G$ of a regular dessin of ${\mathcal K}_{2^e,2^f}$ admits an exact bicyclic factorization $G=\langle b\rangle\langle w\rangle$ of type $(2^e,2^f)$ with $\langle b\rangle\cap\langle w\rangle=1$. For a fixed group $G$, two exact generating pairs give isomorphic dessins exactly when they lie in the same orbit under ${\rm A}ut(G)$. Thus the classification reduces to three group-theoretic tasks: determining the isomorphism classes of the possible groups $G$, characterizing their exact bicyclic generating pairs, and computing $|{\rm A}ut(G)|$. Berkovich and Janko divided the relevant non-metacyclic groups, through parameterized presentations, according to whether the commutator subgroup is cyclic, contains a cyclic subgroup of index $2$, or contains a cyclic subgroup of index $2^r$ with $r>1$. However, their classification does not identify which parameter values in these presentations define isomorphic groups; this problem was raised by Janko in {J}. We carry out these steps for the cyclic-commutator case. This settles Janko's isomorphism-classification problem in this case and yields a complete classification and enumeration of the corresponding regular dessins.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-29T05:44:15Z</published>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39345v1</id>
    <title>Stopping Rules and the Poisson Boundary of Random Walks on Countable Groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-29T04:34:10Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39345v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39345v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>In this paper, we study the terminal laws and Poisson boundaries obtained by stopping random walks on countable groups. For a transient walk, we give a direct Green-potential characterization of randomized stopping distributions and show that the terminal law determines the mean stopping time. On free groups, this yields finitely supported randomized stopping distributions at a positive total variation distance from every ordinary stopping distribution. We construct symmetric, fully supported recurrent measures of finite entropy on countable locally finite groups and obtain ordinary strict boundary enlargements when the group is not Choquet-Deny. For generating source and terminal measures of finite entropy, positive asymptotic entropy of the source forces the stopping time to have finite mean. A direct proof of the finite-mean entropy formula and boundary preservation then shows that a finite-entropy stopping chain has at most one strict enlargement. An exact stopped-word entropy identity shows that infinite-mean ordinary stopping with a finite-entropy terminal law has infinite conditional history entropy.</summary>
    <category term="math.PR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-29T04:34:10Z</published>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39228v1</id>
    <title>Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation</title>
    <updated>2026-10-29T02:48:58Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39228v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39228v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given.</summary>
    <category term="math.CO" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39033v1</id>
    <title>Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach</title>
    <updated>2026-10-28T23:04:37Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39033v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39033v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichmüller spaces. We further establish large deviation principles for quasimorphisms on countable groups, and for random walks generated by compositions of Euclidean isometries; also, we discuss extensions and streamlining of known large deviation results for singular values of random matrix products. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.</summary>
    <category term="math.PR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38991v1</id>
    <title>Grothendieck Pairs, Functors and Profinite Invariants</title>
    <updated>2026-10-28T22:15:01Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38991v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.38991v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>As another variation of profinite properties, we define the notion of natural profinite invariants: functorial invariants, inducing isomorphisms for every Grothendieck pair. We give a characterisation of when adjoint functors are natural profinite invariants and describe a strategy on how to disprove natural profinite invariance. By means of examples we show that the notions of profinite invariance and natural profinite invariances are logically independent.</summary>
